title: Anthropic IPO, the largest AI listing
since_label: Tue 10 Nov, when the price range was set
status: Bloomberg and CNN report ANT opened at $111.50 on Thu 19 Nov and closed at $97.17, 17% above the $83 IPO price, with CNN putting the fully diluted value at $1.76T while Yahoo Finance puts it at about $1.27T based on shares outstanding. CNBC reports the stock fell 9% at Friday's open amid a wider AI sell-off, and Bloomberg reports the Nasdaq 100 closed down 2.2% on debut day; where the stock settles after the first-day pop is still open.
why: A raise this size absorbs cash that would otherwise chase other risk, and its first-day close reprices every AI name.
sources: Bloomberg, CNN, CNBC, Yahoo Finance, Reuters, Forbes

title: Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO, Kress named interim
since_label: Fri 6 Nov close, the last price before the weekend reports
status: The Guardian, citing Bloomberg, reports the board's recruiter Heidrick & Struggles has approached Arm CEO Rene Haas, with Ian Buck, Lisa Su and Johny Srouji also named as possible candidates, and reports Nvidia has tried to curb talk of a Huang return after he said he would be willing to come back. Yahoo Finance reports the shares fell about 3% on Fri 20 Nov and are down 14% since the resignation, and no permanent CEO has been named.
why: Nvidia is the anchor of the AI trade and one of the heaviest weights in the Nasdaq, which alts follow.
sources: Nvidia, Bloomberg, The Guardian, Yahoo Finance, CNBC, Reuters

title: Iran and US trade strikes in the Gulf
since_label: Thu 12 Nov 00:00 UTC, before Iran reported the Sirik strike
status: CBS News, citing Reuters, reports Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed two more tankers hit mines in Hormuz on Thu 19 Nov, and Bloomberg reports CENTCOM widened the blockade on Wed to cover ship-to-ship transfers after the first observed transfer of Iranian crude near Kharg. Iran International and Al Jazeera report Guards-linked media are urging Iran to send a tanker convoy through the blockade and threatening Gulf oil sites if the tankers are attacked; Iran has not confirmed a plan, and no ceasefire has been reported.
why: CoinDesk cites the Gulf escalation, with the dollar and Fed hike odds, behind the crypto sell-off; oil feeds straight into rate expectations.
sources: CBS News, Reuters, Bloomberg, Al Jazeera, Iran International, CoinDesk

title: MSCI drops Strategy from its indexes
since_label: Wed 11 Nov close, before MSCI's after-hours announcement
status: Bitcoin Magazine reports Strategy fell 4.6% to $86.13 on Thu 19 Nov, a sixth straight loss, as bitcoin touched $61,658, and CoinGlass data show $582M of net US spot ETF outflows that day. Investing.com puts the passive selling due before the deletion after the close on 30 Nov at about $1.6B and BitcoinWorld puts it at $2B to $3B; whether other index providers will follow is still open.
why: Strategy is the largest corporate BTC holder, and forced selling of its shares tests the main route equity money takes into bitcoin.
sources: MSCI, Strategy, Bitcoin Magazine, Investing.com, CoinGlass, Benzinga, The Block

title: Binance $6.3B hack, stolen ETH on the move
since_label: Thu 29 Oct 00:00 UTC, before the hack was reported
status: Cointelegraph, citing Onchain Lens, reports the hacker moved another 197,460 ETH, about $346M, on Fri 20 Nov after 137,602 ETH on Thu, routing part of it through THORChain and Chainflip, and says Arkham data show about 225,000 ETH left in the tracked addresses. Binance says it has reimbursed customers and is pursuing a worldwide freezing order in Abu Dhabi, where a hearing on 1 Dec will decide whether 18 firms must hand over assets they have frozen.
why: Stolen ETH that no issuer can freeze is being moved and swapped, a supply overhang for ETH and alts while crypto sentiment sits at extreme fear.
next_label: Abu Dhabi court hearing on frozen assets
sources: Binance, Reuters, CoinDesk, Cointelegraph, Crypto Times, The Block
